title: The idea the filter missed
lines: A research filter rejects an unfamiliar idea; was it weak, or simply hard to recognize?
Novelty That Resembles the Past investigates whether AI research filters discard the differences that make an idea new.
It begins by separating three questions: is an idea new, is it useful, and is it true?

title: A difference lost in summary
lines: A summary can keep a proposal’s subject while losing the assumption that made it different.
The book follows how that difference can disappear as an idea moves toward evaluation.
Its proposed experiments ask how to test a preference for familiar ideas without assuming the answer.

title: Room for the unfamiliar
lines: Anyone whose work resists familiar categories will recognize the stakes of being understood before being ranked.
